name: Ahiam
overview: Ahiam was a male figure known as the son of Sharar and identified as the twenty-sixth member of the elite group known as "the thirty," who were valiant warriors serving under King David. While his tribal affiliation and additional personal details are not recorded, his inclusion among David's mighty men highlights his role in the military leadership during David's reign.
namesAndTitles: The name Ahiam means "brother of mother," a proper name recorded in 2 Samuel 23:33. This name does not appear to have been given by God but reflects a familial connection implied in its meaning.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Ahiam was the son of Sharar, as noted in 2 Samuel 23:33. Beyond this paternal link, no further family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Ahiam's significance lies in his membership among "the thirty," a distinguished group of David's warriors known for their bravery and loyalty. His position as the twenty-sixth of these men underscores his contribution to the military strength that supported David's kingdom. Though not extensively detailed, his mention affirms the collective valor and leadership that characterized David's reign.
